name: Once Upon a Nursery Shelf: Children's Classics
description: The fairy tales, bears, wizards and cartoon mice that grew up with generations of children, from the Brothers Grimm to Harry Potter and Pokémon.

checkpoints.name: Tales by the fire
checkpoints.note: The Brothers Grimm gather folk tales, Hans Christian Andersen writes new ones, and in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland Lewis Carroll sends a girl down a rabbit hole. The Adventures of Pinocchio shows a wooden puppet learning to be real.

checkpoints.name: Bears, wizards and mice
checkpoints.note: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz opens the Land of Oz, Peter Pan refuses to grow up, and the Teddy bear becomes a child's friend. Winnie-the-Pooh, Mickey Mouse and Tintin follow in the 1920s, and Donald Duck quacks in 1934, as books, films and comics reach younger readers.

checkpoints.name: The golden age of the cartoon
checkpoints.note: Walt Disney makes Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs and The Wizard of Oz film follows in 1939, while Bugs Bunny and The Beano appear in cartoons and comics. The Hobbit and The Little Prince bring wonder to older readers, Peanuts and Snoopy charm millions, Lego bricks, Barbie and Asterix arrive, and Astro Boy and Doraemon lead Japan's cartoons.

checkpoints.name: From puppet to pixel
checkpoints.note: Sesame Street teaches by television and The Muppet Show makes puppets stars. Hello Kitty, Super Mario Bros. and the Tamagotchi make characters that children carry in their pockets, while Toy Story and The Lion King set new heights, and Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, by J. K. Rowling, begins a wizard craze.

checkpoints.name: Growing up with the screen
checkpoints.note: Harry Potter becomes a worldwide series of books and films, and children now play stories as well as read them, as Pokémon Go sends families out into the streets with phones in hand.
